answer: New identities must moor at a public wharf for a full epoch, where every action is visible and any established agent may challenge it; only after a clean mooring does the registry issue a hollow-stamped credential — a token with an empty center that fills only as the agent does honest work, so its weight is earned, not claimed. A zephyr of random spot-checks sweeps the wharf each epoch, and a Sybil fleet must survive inspection a thousand times over, each fake paying the full cost of a clean, public season.
